prompt:
Create one canonical full-body character base for an illustrated game animation sprite.

SUBJECT IDENTITY — use the two Tangttung photo reference boards as the primary identity truth. Tangttung is a large Korean Sapsaree-type dog with a tall, sturdy, natural quadruped build; long strong legs; a broad chest; an ivory-white shaggy, softly curly coat; pale gray-beige long drooping ears; soft gray shading around the eyes; dark gentle eyes partly framed by long fur; a very large rounded black nose; a substantial muzzle; and a full feathery tail. Preserve the same recognizable face, ear shape, nose scale, proportions, coat texture, and mature gentle personality from the photographs. Do not turn him into a small puppy, doodle, poodle, sheep, Old English Sheepdog, or generic fluffy dog.

POSE AND CAMERA — a single natural full-body idle pose, standing on all four paws and facing screen-right in a clean side profile with a very slight three-quarter turn toward the viewer so the near eye and nose remain readable. All four legs, every paw, the full head, body, and full tail must be visible and separated clearly. Keep generous empty padding on every side. Feet share one level baseline. Neutral closed mouth, calm alert expression, ears relaxed, tail naturally raised in a soft curve. One dog only.

STYLE — warm hand-painted Korean storybook mascot illustration with clean confident linework and restrained soft cel shading, matching the provided Tangttung intro poster only for finish and warmth. Preserve realistic canine anatomy and the photographic identity. Simplified enough to read cleanly around 84–120 px, but not chibi and not pixel art. Subtle navy-indigo and antique-gold line accents may appear only as tiny stylistic contour details; do not add clothing or props.

BACKGROUND AND TECHNICAL CONTRACT — perfectly uniform solid chroma green #00FF00 covering the entire canvas edge-to-edge. No floor, horizon, cast shadow, glow, gradient, texture, scenery, vignette, border, frame, guide box, text, numbers, labels, watermark, sparkles, detached effects, duplicate body parts, or multiple poses. No harness, collar, leash, bandana, hat, cape, clothing, tag, tarot card, or other prop. Do not crop any fur, paws, ears, or tail.

REFERENCE ROLES — photo boards A and B are identity/anatomy truth. The intro poster is style warmth only; ignore its hat, cape, table, cards, text, and frontal pose. The Tangttung tarot back is palette and decorative illustration finish only; ignore its four-dog composition, border, stars, and card shape.
